rules.council_observation: Read in full (owner-supplied copy, pinned as JASPER_MILLER_2011; the Supporting Information was not supplied). The paper compares ways of modelling the CH4 + M interaction against full-dimensional direct dynamics for He, Ne and H2 (direct dynamics was also run for CH4, with nothing to compare it to). The reference is a validated low-level surface (MP2, or scaled-correlation SAC for H2), not an exact one. For He and Ne an exp/6 pairwise potential reproduces the direct-dynamics deactivating-collision average closely; a Lennard-Jones one overshoots it, tested for He only, at 300-2000 K (the paper expects the deficiency to be general, p. 6447); for H2, N2 and CO the pairwise form is too inflexible and its parametrisation adds an uncertainty the paper states as 20-40 %, 10-50 % or up to 50 % in different places. The transfer averages did not depend on the intramolecular potential (shown for He and Ne only). The comparison is a fidelity-to-a-model claim: only the paper's final CH4 rates against experiment are physical accuracy, registered separately as N-JM-CH4-RATE.
